why: The score depends only on the size of each connected component. Union-find with size tracking merges the endpoints of every edge, then each root contributes ceil(sqrt(size)).
hints: The answer only needs component sizes, not the components themselves.
Union-find by size: every edge merges two components and adds their sizes at the new root.
Union all edges, then for each node that is its own root add ceil(sqrt(size)), computed exactly as isqrt(size - 1) + 1. O((n + m) alpha(n)).
pitfalls: Isolated nodes are components of size 1 and contribute 1 each.
Floating-point sqrt can misround for perfect squares; use integer isqrt.
Nodes are 1-based; edges may repeat or close cycles, so skip unions within one component.
statement:
An undirected graph has nodes 1 to n. Its edges are given as two equal-length arrays: edge i joins graphFrom[i] and graphTo[i].

Find every connected component (a node with no edges is a component of size 1). For each component of size s, take ceil(sqrt(s)), and return the sum over all components.

Example. n = 6, graphFrom = [1,2,4], graphTo = [2,3,5].

  1. Edges 1-2 and 2-3 form {1,2,3}, size 3: ceil(sqrt(3)) = 2.
  2. Edge 4-5 forms {4,5}, size 2: ceil(sqrt(2)) = 2.
  3. Node 6 alone, size 1: ceil(sqrt(1)) = 1.

Sum: 2 + 2 + 1 = 5.
